svg.text: POISONING AND OVERDOSE — WHAT NOT TO DO FIRST
Treat the patient, not the poison. Airway, breathing and circulation come before any antidote.

g.text: Do not make the patient vomit
Do not give salt water or milk
Do not give anything by mouth to a
Do not lavage a corrosive or a
or plant — bring it with the patient

svg.text: THREE PATTERNS SEEN IN GHANAIAN WARDS

g.text: ORGANOPHOSPHATE, from farm pesticide — wet everywhere: salivation, tears, urine, small pupils, wheeze
PARACETAMOL — looks completely well for a day or two, then the liver fails. Treat on the history, not the look
CAUSTIC SODA or acid — mouth burns, drooling, pain on swallowing. Nothing by mouth, no tube, urgent referral

svg.text: EVERY DELIBERATE OVERDOSE NEEDS A MENTAL HEALTH ASSESSMENT
Attempted suicide was decriminalised in Ghana in 2023. The person needs assessment and care, not the police.
A patient who looks well after an overdose is not necessarily safe. Some poisons declare themselves late.
